cohort: The cohort consisted of 685 patients who underwent cesarean sections between January 2021 and December 2023, categorized into infection (n=33) and non-infection (n=652) groups.
finding: Key risk factors for postoperative infections following cesarean sections were identified as excessive vaginal examinations, membrane rupture, cervical dilation, diabetes mellitus, and GBS colonization, and a nomogram was developed with strong predictive accuracy and clinical utility.
mod_finding: The study specifically focused on postoperative infections following cesarean sections, analyzing risk factors within this particular mode of birth.
